posts.title: What I Learned Designing a Semantic Layer for a $2B Defense Program
posts.excerpt: A semantic layer isn't just a tech artifact - it's a contract between the people who measure things and the people who decide things. Here's what made ours stick across six departments.
posts.body:
When we set out to build a real-time BI platform at Austal USA, the tech stack wasn't the hard part. The hard part was getting QA, production, procurement, and finance to agree on what 'on-time delivery' meant. The semantic layer became the negotiating table.

Three principles that survived contact with reality:

1. Every KPI gets one definition, owned by one team. No exceptions.
2. The transformation logic lives in version control, not someone's notebook.
3. Lineage is documented automatically, never by hand.

posts.title: How We Cut ETL Latency from 10 Minutes to Under 2 Seconds
posts.excerpt: Sub-2-second BI on multi-source operational data isn't about throwing Spark at the problem. It's a series of unglamorous engineering decisions stacked carefully.
posts.body: Going from 10-minute manual prep to live data was a full-stack engineering exercise: incremental ingestion, columnar storage layout, careful indexing, and Kubernetes-managed parallel clusters that scale during audit windows. The biggest unlock wasn't any single tool - it was shrinking the work each layer had to do.

posts.title: ISO 9001 Compliance, but for Your Data Pipeline
posts.excerpt: Audit-ready data lineage shouldn't slow you down - it should be a side effect of building things right. Here's the framework we used.
posts.body: ISO 9001 cares about traceability, repeatability, and corrective action. Data engineering already cares about all three - we just don't usually call it that. We mapped automated lineage tracking, schema versioning, and PySpark validation pipelines onto the audit checklist and turned a compliance burden into a free byproduct of good engineering.
